title: Every Grove Liquidity Layer allocation is specified by an Instance Configuration Document with the same five-part parameter schema
content:
Across A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.10.1 (Ripple RLUSD), .11.1 (Agora AUSD), .12.1/.12.2/.12.3 (three Uniswap v3 AUSD/USDC Instances) and .13.1 (Maple syrupUSDC), every allocation is described by an "Instance Configuration Document" carrying an identical subtree:

1. **Instance Identifiers** — Network, Target Protocol, *Asset Supplied By Grove Liquidity Layer*, Token
2. **Contract Addresses** — token, underlying asset, and where relevant deposit/withdrawal/pool addresses
3. **Rate Limit IDs** — the on-chain `RateLimitID` hashes for inflow and outflow
4. **Rate Limits** — `maxAmount` and `slope` per direction
5. **Off-chain Operational Parameters**, plus optional *Instance-specific Operational Processes* and *Instance-specific Operational Parameters*

The last two slots are explicitly defined as escape hatches: they "contain operational procedures or monitoring requirements unique to this Instance that **deviate from or otherwise supplement** the general Grove Liquidity Layer processes."

The design choice is uniformity-with-exceptions. Lending pools, a stablecoin issuer conduit, and an AMM LP position have almost nothing in common economically, yet all are forced into one schema so that a reviewer can compare them line-by-line and diff a proposed change against the prior state. The cost is that genuinely venue-specific risk controls (TWAP windows, slippage bounds, tick ranges) get pushed into the free-form "Instance-specific" appendix, where they are structurally invisible to anyone scanning only the common fields.
description: Identifiers, contract addresses, RateLimitIDs, rate limits and off-chain parameters repeat verbatim across Ripple, Agora, Uniswap and Maple Instances, making heterogeneous venues diffable.
